Hello, community! 🎄

How it's December already? [This time last year](https://secure.campaigner.com/CSB/Public/archive.aspx?args=ODAxOTQ4MjI%3d&acc=NzcwMzg0) we were sharing some of our very first activities and the first blog post we've written with the Knowledge Mobilization Hub. One year later, we have participated in a handful of institutional, national or international events, launched our Open Scholarship Champions program, revamped our website, created a lot of resources, and, most importantly, we are more and more mindful and aware about our community needs and desires, our institutional infrastructure to support open scholarship practices, and learning together how to advocate for the culture change we want to see. And we are so, so happy that you're sticking around with us!

Happy reading!

## This newsletter is now open


#### Made in the open, with you

This newsletter is now written, reviewed and published openly on GitHub, the
same way we encourage open research. Every issue's source, its review and
what was sent are public, and anyone can reuse the template under a CC BY 4.0
licence.

**Have news to share?** An event, a project, a funding call or a resource:
tell us through a short online form, and we'll consider it for an upcoming
issue. Submissions are public, so only share what can be published. You'll
need a free GitHub account; if you'd rather not do it through GitHub, email us at
[open_scholarship@sfu.ca](mailto:open_scholarship@sfu.ca).

[Share your news](https://github.com/open-scholarship-sfu/newsletter/issues/new/choose){.button}
[See how it's made](https://github.com/open-scholarship-sfu/newsletter){.button .secondary}


## Celebrating Open Education at SFU

::: {.feature image="https://placehold.co/600x400/000000/FFFFFF.png" alt="Describe the image" link="https://..."}

On November 10th we gathered at the Burnaby Library for a lunch to celebrate those using, producing, sharing or just curious about open educational resources and practices. We heard from Evan Acetolla about engaging students in producing open educational resources, from Juan Pablo Alperin about how his experience in the back-end of open publishing shaped his career and teaching practices, from Stephanie Bertels about the open educational products that have been used to improve companies' sustainability strategies, and from Jessica Lamb about the impacts of textbooks costs on students' education and how open resources can mitigate that. The event was co-organized with the Open Education Community of Practice.

We congratulate and appreciate all the open education champions in our community! Thank you! ♥️

[Read the story](https://...){.button}

[Join the Open Education Community of Practice](https://canvas.sfu.ca/enroll/3H3PHW)
:::

## We've been busy!

::: two-col
::: {.col}
### 2nd Canadian Open Science Conference

In October the Open Scholar Champions from SFU joined a wider Canadian community on the [2nd Canadian Open Science Conference](https://carn-recar.ca/2nd-canadian-open-science-conference/) in Ottawa, ON. Our community shared insights about the intersections between AI and Open Scholarship and [our strategy to map SFU's resources and infrastructure to support open scholarship practices](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24179638). Together with the TOSI Alliance, we presented results of two of our working groups: one about standards in neuro data sharing and another about [curation of training resources for neuro open science](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23481124).


:::

:::{.col}
### SORTEE Conference 2026

We were also present at the 2026 edition of the global and online conference of the [Society for Open, Reliable, and Transparent Ecology and Evolutionary Biology (SORTEE)](https://sortee.org/). Our community manager hosted an unconference where she provoked participants to analyse if we could use metrics and concepts from Ecology and Evolution to understand and evaluate open scholarship practices. [Materials are openly published](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24183615) and can be reused under CC-BY license.
:::
:::

#### NASA Open Science reopens training

From the [NASA Open Science Newsletter](https://science.nasa.gov/open-science/):

> NASA's Open Science Essentials ([OSE](https://stemgateway.nasa.gov/s/course-offering/a0BSJ0000049icD/open-science-essentials)) and Open Science 101 ([OS101](https://stemgateway.nasa.gov/s/course-offering/a0BSJ0000049ih3/open-science-101)) courses are currently accepting new learners.

Enrolment is open until capacity is reached. This training is accepted as prerequisite to become an Open Scholarship Champion at SFU and it's free.
:::

## Resources

- [OS in the research life cycle](https://www.sfu.ca/research/researcher-resources/further-my-research/open-scholarship.html): we have included on our website an extensive list of resources, infrastructure information and support guides to help you navigate open scholarship practices at SFU.
- [The Sharing Shift](https://sharingshift.okfn.org/): the Open Knowledge Foundation and [CNRS](https://cis.cnrs.fr/) have launched a project to keep the digital commons open without leaving them open to extraction by AI. Through new licences, governance models and legal strategies, it aims to give people who share data and knowledge real control over how it’s used. 

## See you in 2027! ❄️

That's it for this month! We hope you enjoy a cozy holiday break and that you feel the joy of the shared commons in your heart.

We are preparing a lot of new things for the next term, including focus groups where you'll get to help us stress-test our support system for each stage of the research life cycle. We're also excited to see what our Open Scholarship Champions will do next, the events that'll come up in the summer... So much to look forward to! [Get in touch with us](mailto:open_scholarship@sfu.ca) if you want to get involved!

We deeply appreciate your engagement with our community throughout 2026 and we look forward to collaborating with you in 2027! Every click on this newsletter and every message we get tell us that we're on the right track to a more inclusive, transparent and responsible research culture at SFU.

See you in January!
